candidates.original_title: Transcriptional amplification in tumor cells with elevated c-Myc
candidates.description: c-Myc overexpression increases total RNA levels in P493-6 Burkitt's lymphoma cells
candidates.citation_sentence: This experiment is similar to what was reported in Figure 3E of Lin et al. (2012) and used the same extraction method for total RNA quantification, which was described in Protocol 2 in the Registered Report (Blum et al., 2015).
candidates.notes: Results mixed across two serum lots: serum lot one not significant (p=0.347), serum lot two significant (p=0.0024). Meta-analysis barely significant (p=0.0488). Authors state results are 'consistent when considering the direction of the effect' but note substantial within-study variation and that point estimates for the two serum lots are not within each other's confidence intervals. candidates.original_title: Transcriptional amplification in tumor cells with elevated c-Myc
candidates.description: c-Myc overexpression amplifies gene expression of active genes but not silent genes in P493-6 Burkitt's lymphoma cells
candidates.citation_sentence: This experiment is similar to what was reported in Figure 3F and Table S1 of Lin et al. (2012) and described in Protocols 3–4 in the Registered Report (Blum et al., 2015).
candidates.notes: Active genes show significant increases consistent with original, but silent genes also show significant increases for some comparisons (0hr vs 1hr and 0hr vs 24hr) unlike the original which found no significant change in silent genes. Authors use hedging language: 'suggest that while both active and silent genes increased in expression upon c-Myc induction, the rate of increase was different.' Meta-analyses show heterogeneity between original and replication studies. [ling26: extra entry, not in the external record]
